english: don’t live one way in private and another in public

terms.latin: Nōn vīvēs aliter in sōlitūdine, aliter in forō.
evidence: De moribus 32: Nōn vīvēs aliter in forō, aliter in sōlitūdine.
terms.comment: From the anonymous collection of maxims once ascribed to Seneca (Dē mōribus), with the two places in the other order; it also stands among the prose sentences printed after Publilius in the Latin Library text. Not Seneca’s own.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
The pseudo-Senecan De moribus 32, quoted from the Latin Library texts (CLTK mirror); not in Lewis & Short or the loci collections.
